title: Level 1 project: a grade book
lesson:
Put Level 1 together like a real problem set: a **grade book** for a class, built as a class you could later put behind a window or a phone screen.

Make `public class GradeBook` with:
1. `addScore(String student, int score)`: tidy the name (trim, first letter capital, rest lower), refuse scores below 0 or above 100 with `IllegalArgumentException`, and store it. A student can have many scores.
2. `average(String student)`: the student's average, rounded to 1 decimal; 0.0 if they have no scores.
3. `best()`: the name of the student with the highest average ("" if empty).
4. `report()`: one line per student in alphabetical order, `Name: average`, joined with newlines, e.g. `Amina: 85.0\nJuma: 72.5`.

Plan first: what field holds the data? (A `TreeMap<String, ArrayList<Integer>>` gives alphabetical order for free.) Write the method headers with a comment each, then build and check them one at a time.

Next: **Level 2** (interfaces, inheritance, collections in depth, testing with JUnit) when it's ready.

notes: computeIfAbsent makes the list the first time a name appears, then adds to it.

exercises.title: The grade book
exercises.prompt: Build GradeBook with addScore, average, best and report as described in the lesson. All the tests must pass, including hidden ones.

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { GradeBook g = new GradeBook(); g.addScore(" amina ", 80); g.addScore("AMINA", 90); g.addScore("juma", 72); g.addScore("Juma", 73); return g.average("Amina") + " " + g.average("Juma"); }).get()
tests.name: averages

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { GradeBook g = new GradeBook(); g.addScore("juma", 72); g.addScore("amina", 85); return g.best(); }).get()
tests.name: best

tests.call: ((java.util.function.Supplier<String>) () -> { GradeBook g = new GradeBook(); g.addScore("juma", 72); g.addScore("amina", 85); return g.report().replace("\n", "|"); }).get()
tests.name: report

tests.hint_if_fail: Scores above 100 or below 0 must throw IllegalArgumentException.

hints: Field: private final TreeMap<String, ArrayList<Integer>> scores = new TreeMap<>();
best: loop over scores.keySet(), keep the name with the highest average(name).
report: StringBuilder; for each name append name + ": " + average(name), with "\n" between lines.

choices: Each name maps to its list of scores, and the names stay alphabetical
quiz.why: Right shape for the data, order for free.

quiz.q: Where should 'scores must be 0-100' be enforced?
choices: In addScore, so bad data never gets in
quiz.why: Guard the data at the door.

quiz.q: Before writing a bigger class you should…
choices: Plan the fields and method headers first
quiz.why: Plan, then build one method at a time.

cards.q: Make a list in a map the first time a key appears?

cards.a: In the method that stores it.

explain: Explain level 1 project: a grade book to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
